title: Host Assigned to Default VLAN Instead of Department VLAN
symptom: PC-1 in Finance department (192.168.10.50) cannot ping Finance Default Gateway 192.168.10.1 on Router R1.
topology_notes: PC-1 connects to Switch SW1 interface Fa0/1. SW1 connects to Router R1 on G0/1 (VLAN 10 Sub-interface). Expected VLAN: 10 (Finance).
show_commands:
SW1# show vlan brief
VLAN Name                             Status    Ports
---- -------------------------------- --------- -------------------------------
1    default                          active    Fa0/1, Fa0/3, Fa0/4, Fa0/5
10   Finance                          active    Fa0/2
20   Sales                            active    Fa0/6
99   Management                       active    

SW1# show interfaces FastEthernet0/1 switchport
Name: Fa0/1
Switchport: Enabled
Administrative Mode: static access
Operational Mode: static access
Access Mode VLAN: 1 (default)
Trunking Native Mode VLAN: 1 (default)
actual_root_cause: Switch port Fa0/1 is assigned to Default VLAN 1 instead of VLAN 10 (Finance).

title: Trunk Port Allowed VLAN List Missing Department VLAN 20
symptom: Hosts in Sales VLAN 20 on Switch SW2 cannot communicate with Sales server on Switch SW1 across trunk link G0/1.
topology_notes: SW1 and SW2 connected via GigabitEthernet0/1 802.1Q trunk. VLANs 10, 20, 30 active on both switches.
show_commands:
SW1# show interfaces trunk
Port        Mode             Encapsulation  Status        Native vlan
Gi0/1       on               802.1q         trunking      1

Port        Vlans allowed on trunk
Gi0/1       10,30

Port        Vlans allowed and active in management domain
Gi0/1       10,30

Port        Vlans in spanning tree forwarding state and not pruned
Gi0/1       10,30
actual_root_cause: Trunk interface Gi0/1 on SW1 has a restricted allowed VLAN list (10,30) that omits VLAN 20.

title: Native VLAN Mismatch on Inter-Switch Trunk Link
symptom: CDP native VLAN mismatch warning messages on console; untagged management traffic is leaking into production VLAN.
topology_notes: SW1 and SW2 connected via Trunk on Fa0/24. SW1 configured with native VLAN 10, SW2 configured with native VLAN 99.
show_commands:
SW1# show interfaces FastEthernet0/24 trunk
Port        Mode             Encapsulation  Status        Native vlan
Fa0/24      desirable        802.1q         trunking      10

SW2# show interfaces FastEthernet0/24 trunk
Port        Mode             Encapsulation  Status        Native vlan
Fa0/24      desirable        802.1q         trunking      99

%CDP-4-NATIVE_VLAN_MISMATCH: Native VLAN mismatch discovered on FastEthernet0/24 (10), with SW2 FastEthernet0/24 (99).
actual_root_cause: Native VLAN configuration mismatch across trunk link Fa0/24 (SW1 is set to Native VLAN 10, SW2 is set to Native VLAN 99).

title: Access Port Configured for Non-Existent VLAN ID
symptom: PC-2 on Fa0/5 has link light amber/inactive and cannot send or receive any frames.
topology_notes: PC-2 intended for HR VLAN 50. Switch SW1.
show_commands:
SW1# show running-config interface FastEthernet0/5
interface FastEthernet0/5
 switchport access vlan 50
 switchport mode access
!

SW1# show vlan brief
VLAN Name                             Status    Ports
---- -------------------------------- --------- -------------------------------
1    default                          active    Fa0/1, Fa0/2, Fa0/3, Fa0/4
10   Finance                          active    
20   Sales                            active    

SW1# show interfaces FastEthernet0/5 status
Port      Name               Status       Vlan       Duplex  Speed Type
Fa0/5                        inactive     50           auto   auto 10/100BaseTX
actual_root_cause: VLAN 50 has not been created in the switch VLAN database, causing interface Fa0/5 to remain inactive.

title: Subnet Mask Mismatch on Router Default Gateway Interface
symptom: Hosts with IPs 192.168.1.130-192.168.1.200 cannot ping their default gateway 192.168.1.1, while hosts 192.168.1.2-192.168.1.100 can.
topology_notes: LAN Subnet intended to be /24 (255.255.255.0). Router R1 G0/0 interface is gateway.
show_commands:
R1# show ip interface GigabitEthernet0/0
GigabitEthernet0/0 is up, line protocol is up
  Internet address is 192.168.1.1/25
  Broadcast address is 192.168.1.127
  Address determined by setup command
  MTU is 1500 bytes

PC-1# ipconfig
IP Address......................: 192.168.1.150
Subnet Mask.....................: 255.255.255.0
Default Gateway.................: 192.168.1.1
actual_root_cause: Router interface G0/0 is configured with subnet mask /25 (255.255.255.128) instead of /24, isolating hosts in the upper half of the /24 subnet.

title: Switch Unreachable from Remote Subnet Due to Missing Default Gateway
symptom: Administrator from Network 10.0.0.0/24 can ping PC-1 (192.168.1.10) but cannot SSH/ping Switch SW1 Management IP 192.168.1.2.
topology_notes: SW1 has Management VLAN 1 IP 192.168.1.2/24. Router R1 is at 192.168.1.1.
show_commands:
SW1# show ip interface brief
Interface              IP-Address      OK? Method Status                Protocol
Vlan1                  192.168.1.2     YES manual up                    up

SW1# show running-config | include default-gateway
(No output returned)

SW1# show ip route
Default gateway is not set
actual_root_cause: Switch SW1 is missing the `ip default-gateway 192.168.1.1` command, preventing return traffic to remote subnets.

title: Host Configured with Incorrect Default Gateway IP Address
symptom: PC-Admin can communicate with local LAN devices but cannot access any remote servers or the Internet.
topology_notes: Local LAN 172.16.10.0/24. Router R1 interface G0/0 IP is 172.16.10.1.
show_commands:
PC-Admin> ipconfig
FastEthernet0 Connection:
   Link-local IPv6 Address.........: fe80::201:42ff:fe28:1a01
   IP Address......................: 172.16.10.15
   Subnet Mask.....................: 255.255.255.0
   Default Gateway.................: 172.16.10.254

R1# show ip interface brief
Interface              IP-Address      OK? Method Status                Protocol
GigabitEthernet0/0     172.16.10.1     YES manual up                    up
actual_root_cause: PC-Admin is statically configured with non-existent default gateway 172.16.10.254 instead of 172.16.10.1.

title: HSRP Virtual IP Address Mismatch Between Dual Gateways
symptom: Hosts experience intermittent gateway drops; both R1 and R2 claim active gateway status for different virtual IPs.
topology_notes: HSRP Group 1 on LAN 192.168.1.0/24. Intended Virtual IP (VIP): 192.168.1.254.
show_commands:
R1# show standby brief
                     P indicates configured to preempt.
                     |
Interface   Grp  Pri P State   Active          Standby         Virtual IP
Gi0/0       1    110 P Active  local           192.168.1.3     192.168.1.254

R2# show standby brief
                     P indicates configured to preempt.
                     |
Interface   Grp  Pri P State   Active          Standby         Virtual IP
Gi0/0       1    100   Active  local           unknown         192.168.1.250
actual_root_cause: HSRP standby group 1 virtual IP mismatch: R1 is configured for 192.168.1.254 while R2 is configured for 192.168.1.250.

title: Client Obtains 169.254.x.x (APIPA) Due to Missing DHCP Pool
symptom: All newly connected workstations show 169.254.x.x APIPA addresses and cannot communicate on the network.
topology_notes: Router R1 serves as local DHCP server for LAN 192.168.50.0/24.
show_commands:
PC-1> ipconfig
FastEthernet0 Connection:
   IP Address......................: 169.254.120.45
   Subnet Mask.....................: 255.255.0.0
   Default Gateway.................: 0.0.0.0

R1# show ip dhcp pool
(No DHCP pools configured)

R1# show ip dhcp binding
(No bindings found)
actual_root_cause: No DHCP pool has been configured on Router R1 for subnet 192.168.50.0/24.

title: IP Address Conflict Caused by Missing DHCP Excluded Addresses
symptom: Console logs show duplicate IP address detected for 192.168.1.1; default gateway becomes intermittently unreachable.
show_commands:
R1# show running-config | section dhcp
ip dhcp pool LAN_POOL
 network 192.168.1.0 255.255.255.0
 default-router 192.168.1.1
 dns-server 8.8.8.8
!

R1# show ip dhcp conflict
IP address        Detection-method   Detection-time
192.168.1.1       Ping               Mar 01 2026 09:12 AM
actual_root_cause: Router R1 is missing `ip dhcp excluded-address 192.168.1.1 192.168.1.10`, causing the DHCP server to assign the router's own gateway IP to clients.

title: Remote Subnet Clients Fail DHCP Due to Missing IP Helper Address
symptom: Clients on LAN 2 (192.168.20.0/24) fail to receive IP addresses from centralized DHCP server (10.1.1.100) on LAN 1.
topology_notes: Router R1 connects LAN 2 via interface G0/1. Centralized DHCP Server is at 10.1.1.100.
show_commands:
R1# show running-config interface GigabitEthernet0/1
interface GigabitEthernet0/1
 ip address 192.168.20.1 255.255.255.0
 duplex auto
 speed auto
!

R1# show ip interface GigabitEthernet0/1 | include Helper
  Helper address is not set
actual_root_cause: Router interface G0/1 is missing `ip helper-address 10.1.1.100` to forward DHCP broadcast DISCOVER messages as unicast to the central DHCP server.

title: DHCP Pool Default Router Option Points to Non-Existent IP
symptom: Clients successfully lease IP 192.168.100.x but have no internet or inter-VLAN access.
topology_notes: Gateway interface R1 G0/0 is 192.168.100.1.
show_commands:
R1# show ip dhcp pool POOL_100
Pool POOL_100 :
 Utilization mark (high/low)    : 100 / 0
 Subnet size (lines)             : 1
 Total addresses                 : 254
 Leased addresses                : 12
 Excluded addresses              : 1
 Pending event                   : none
 1 subnet is currently in the pool :
 Current index        IP address range                    Leased addresses
 192.168.100.13       192.168.100.1    - 192.168.100.254   12

R1# show running-config | section dhcp
ip dhcp pool POOL_100
 network 192.168.100.0 255.255.255.0
 default-router 192.168.100.254
 dns-server 1.1.1.1
actual_root_cause: DHCP pool POOL_100 is handing out `default-router 192.168.100.254` when the router's active IP is 192.168.100.1.

title: Client Configured with Unreachable DNS Server IP
symptom: PC-1 can ping web server by IP (172.16.0.10) but browser reports 'Server Not Found' when accessing http://internal.corp.
topology_notes: Corporate DNS server is at 10.0.0.53.
show_commands:
PC-1> ipconfig /all
FastEthernet0 Connection:
   IP Address......................: 192.168.1.10
   Subnet Mask.....................: 255.255.255.0
   Default Gateway.................: 192.168.1.1
   DNS Servers.....................: 10.0.0.35

PC-1> ping 10.0.0.35
Pinging 10.0.0.35 with 32 bytes of data:
Request timed out.
Request timed out.
actual_root_cause: Client DNS server is misconfigured with unreachable IP 10.0.0.35 instead of correct server IP 10.0.0.53.

title: Typo in Router Local Host Name Resolution Table
symptom: Router admin typing 'ping logserver' fails with unknown host or pings incorrect host 10.0.0.250.
topology_notes: Log server actual IP is 10.0.0.25.
show_commands:
R1# show hosts
Default domain is not set
Name/address lookup-tracking disabled
Codes: UN - unknown, EX - expired, OK - OK, ?? - revalidate
       temp - temporary, perm - permanent
       NA - Not Applicable None - Not defined

Host                      Port  Flags      Age Type   Address(es)
logserver                 None  (perm, OK)  0   IP     10.0.0.250

R1# ping logserver
Type escape sequence to abort.
Sending 5, 100-byte ICMP Echos to 10.0.0.250, timeout is 2 seconds:
.....
Success rate is 0 percent (0/5)
actual_root_cause: Static `ip host logserver 10.0.0.250` contains a typo and should point to 10.0.0.25.

title: Extended Ingress ACL Drops DNS UDP Port 53 Traffic
symptom: Branch office PCs cannot resolve external internet domains, but direct IP pings to 8.8.8.8 succeed.
topology_notes: Router R1 WAN interface G0/0 has inbound ACL 105 applied.
show_commands:
R1# show access-lists 105
Extended IP access list 105
    10 permit tcp any any eq www
    20 permit tcp any any eq 443
    30 permit icmp any any (8 matches)
    (Implicit Deny all other traffic)

R1# show ip interface GigabitEthernet0/0 | include access list
  Inbound  access list is 105
  Outbound access list is not set
actual_root_cause: Inbound ACL 105 permits HTTP/HTTPS/ICMP but lacks a rule permitting UDP port 53 DNS responses from external servers.

title: Domain Lookup Disabled on Gateway Router
symptom: Router fails to resolve NTP and Syslog hostnames by FQDN; shows '% Unrecognized host or address'.
topology_notes: Router R1 configured with `ip name-server 8.8.8.8`.
show_commands:
R1# show running-config | include domain|name-server
no ip domain-lookup
ip name-server 8.8.8.8

R1# ping pool.ntp.org
Translating "pool.ntp.org"...domain server (8.8.8.8)
% Unrecognized host or address, or protocol not running.
actual_root_cause: `no ip domain-lookup` is configured, preventing the router IOS from issuing DNS queries to its configured name-server.

title: Missing Default Route on Edge Gateway Router
symptom: Enterprise LAN hosts can reach internal subnets but have zero connectivity to the Internet (e.g. 8.8.8.8).
topology_notes: Edge Router R1 connects to ISP gateway at 203.0.113.1 on G0/1.
show_commands:
R1# show ip route
Codes: L - local, C - connected, S - static, R - RIP, M - mobile, B - BGP
       O - OSPF, IA - OSPF inter area 

Gateway of last resort is not set

      10.0.0.0/8 is variably subnetted, 2 subnets, 2 masks
C        10.1.1.0/24 is directly connected, GigabitEthernet0/0
L        10.1.1.1/32 is directly connected, GigabitEthernet0/0
      203.0.113.0/24 is variably subnetted, 2 subnets, 2 masks
C        203.0.113.0/30 is directly connected, GigabitEthernet0/1
L        203.0.113.2/32 is directly connected, GigabitEthernet0/1
actual_root_cause: Router R1 lacks a default static route (`ip route 0.0.0.0 0.0.0.0 203.0.113.1`) pointing to the ISP gateway.

title: Static Route Configured with Unresolvable Next-Hop IP Typo
symptom: Traffic destined to Branch Office 192.168.30.0/24 is blackholed at Headquarter Router R1.
topology_notes: R1 connected to R2 via point-to-point link 10.0.0.0/30. R2 interface is 10.0.0.2.
show_commands:
R1# show running-config | include ip route
ip route 192.168.30.0 255.255.255.0 10.0.0.6

R1# show ip route 192.168.30.0
% Network not in table

R1# show ip interface brief
Interface              IP-Address      OK? Method Status                Protocol
GigabitEthernet0/0     10.0.0.1        YES manual up                    up
actual_root_cause: Static route specifies invalid next-hop 10.0.0.6 (outside subnet 10.0.0.0/30) instead of 10.0.0.2.

title: OSPF Neighbor Adjacency Fails Due to Hello/Dead Timer Mismatch
symptom: OSPF neighbor state between R1 and R2 stays DOWN; dynamic routes to remote networks are never learned.
topology_notes: R1 G0/0 (10.0.0.1) connects to R2 G0/0 (10.0.0.2) in OSPF Area 0.
show_commands:
R1# show ip ospf interface GigabitEthernet0/0
GigabitEthernet0/0 is up, line protocol is up 
  Internet Address 10.0.0.1/30, Area 0 
  Timer intervals configured, Hello 10, Dead 40, Wait 40, Retransmit 5

R2# show ip ospf interface GigabitEthernet0/0
GigabitEthernet0/0 is up, line protocol is up 
  Internet Address 10.0.0.2/30, Area 0 
  Timer intervals configured, Hello 5, Dead 20, Wait 20, Retransmit 5

R1# show ip ospf neighbor
(No neighbors listed)
actual_root_cause: OSPF Hello/Dead interval mismatch on G0/0 (R1 has 10/40s while R2 has 5/20s), preventing neighbor adjacency formation.

title: OSPF Passive Interface Configured on Active Transit Link
symptom: R1 and R2 cannot form OSPF adjacency across interconnecting link GigabitEthernet0/1.
topology_notes: R1 G0/1 is the transit link to core router R2 in Area 0.
show_commands:
R1# show ip protocols
Routing Protocol is "ospf 1"
  Outgoing update filter list for all interfaces is not set
  Incoming update filter list for all interfaces is not set
  Router ID 1.1.1.1
  Number of areas in this router is 1. 1 normal 0 SSA 0 NSSA
  Maximum path: 4
  Routing for Networks:
    10.0.0.0 0.0.0.3 area 0
    192.168.10.0 0.0.0.255 area 0
  Passive Interface(s):
    GigabitEthernet0/1

R1# show ip ospf neighbor
(No neighbors)
actual_root_cause: GigabitEthernet0/1 is incorrectly configured with `passive-interface`, suppressing OSPF Hello packet transmission to neighbor R2.

title: Standard ACL Filtering by Destination Applied to Outbound Interface
symptom: Finance users cannot access Web Server 10.0.0.5; ACL blocks all traffic because standard ACL matches source IP.
topology_notes: Finance LAN is 192.168.10.0/24. Web Server is 10.0.0.5. Standard ACL 10 applied on R1.
show_commands:
R1# show access-lists 10
Standard IP access list 10
    10 deny   10.0.0.5 (24 matches)
    20 permit any

R1# show running-config interface GigabitEthernet0/1
interface GigabitEthernet0/1
 description Outbound to Web Server LAN
 ip address 10.0.0.1 255.255.255.0
 ip access-group 10 out
!
actual_root_cause: Standard ACL 10 filters source addresses; applying `deny 10.0.0.5` outbound to the 10.0.0.0/24 subnet checks packets coming from 10.0.0.5 rather than destined to it.

title: Implicit Deny All Drops Unlisted Essential Management Protocols
symptom: After applying security ACL 110, engineers cannot SSH or ping Router R1 loopback from the management workstation.
topology_notes: Management PC is 192.168.1.50. Extended ACL 110 applied on R1 G0/0 in.
show_commands:
R1# show access-lists 110
Extended IP access list 110
    10 permit tcp 192.168.1.0 0.0.0.255 any eq 80 (120 matches)
    20 permit tcp 192.168.1.0 0.0.0.255 any eq 443 (340 matches)
    (Implicit Deny all)

R1# show ip interface GigabitEthernet0/0 | include access list
  Inbound  access list is 110
  Outbound access list is not set
actual_root_cause: ACL 110 only permits HTTP/HTTPS; the implicit `deny ip any any` at the end of the list drops SSH (port 22) and ICMP.

title: Inbound Security Policy Mistakenly Bound as Outbound Access Group
symptom: Malicious traffic from untrusted WAN subnet is not being filtered as expected upon entering the router.
topology_notes: WAN link G0/0 connected to untrusted network. Filter ACL 150 intended for ingress.
show_commands:
R1# show running-config interface GigabitEthernet0/0
interface GigabitEthernet0/0
 description WAN Ingress
 ip address 198.51.100.2 255.255.255.0
 ip access-group 150 out
!

R1# show ip interface GigabitEthernet0/0 | include access list
  Inbound  access list is not set
  Outbound access list is 150
actual_root_cause: ACL 150 is applied in the `out` direction instead of `in` on ingress interface GigabitEthernet0/0.

title: Access List Applied to Incorrect Router Interface
symptom: Guest VLAN traffic is able to access Corporate LAN despite ACL 102 being created.
topology_notes: Guest LAN on G0/1. Corporate LAN on G0/2. ACL 102 was bound to G0/0 (Internet).
show_commands:
R1# show running-config interface GigabitEthernet0/0
interface GigabitEthernet0/0
 ip address 203.0.113.1 255.255.255.252
 ip access-group 102 in
!

R1# show running-config interface GigabitEthernet0/1
interface GigabitEthernet0/1
 description Guest LAN
 ip address 172.16.10.1 255.255.255.0
 (No access-group applied)
actual_root_cause: Guest isolation ACL 102 was applied to WAN interface G0/0 instead of Guest interface GigabitEthernet0/1.

title: Dynamic PAT Fails Because Overload Keyword is Missing
symptom: Only one host inside the LAN can access the Internet at a time; all other hosts get connection timeouts.
topology_notes: Inside LAN 192.168.1.0/24 with 50 PCs. Outside interface G0/0 has single public IP 203.0.113.2.
show_commands:
R1# show running-config | include ip nat
ip nat inside source list 1 interface GigabitEthernet0/0
ip nat inside source static 192.168.1.10 203.0.113.10

R1# show access-lists 1
Standard IP access list 1
    10 permit 192.168.1.0 0.0.0.255 (450 matches)

R1# show ip nat translations
Pro Inside global      Inside local       Outside local      Outside global
--- 203.0.113.2        192.168.1.5        ---                ---
actual_root_cause: `ip nat inside source list 1 interface G0/0` is missing the `overload` keyword, enabling 1-to-1 dynamic NAT rather than Port Address Translation (PAT).

title: NAT Inside and Outside Role Definitions Inverted on Interfaces
symptom: No internal LAN clients can translate or reach public servers; `show ip nat translations` is completely blank.
topology_notes: LAN on G0/1 (Inside). ISP WAN on G0/0 (Outside).
show_commands:
R1# show running-config interface GigabitEthernet0/0
interface GigabitEthernet0/0
 description Connected to ISP
 ip address 203.0.113.2 255.255.255.252
 ip nat inside
!

R1# show running-config interface GigabitEthernet0/1
interface GigabitEthernet0/1
 description Connected to LAN
 ip address 192.168.1.1 255.255.255.0
 ip nat outside
!

R1# show ip nat translations
(No translations in table)
actual_root_cause: NAT direction is inverted: `ip nat inside` is assigned to the WAN (G0/0) and `ip nat outside` is assigned to the LAN (G0/1).

title: NAT Access List Excludes Newly Added Department Subnet
symptom: Engineering subnet (192.168.30.0/24) cannot reach the Internet, while HR (192.168.10.0/24) has full Internet access.
topology_notes: Router R1 performs PAT for all internal LANs using ACL 1.
show_commands:
R1# show running-config | include ip nat inside source
ip nat inside source list 1 interface GigabitEthernet0/0 overload

R1# show access-lists 1
Standard IP access list 1
    10 permit 192.168.10.0 0.0.0.255 (1520 matches)
    20 permit 192.168.20.0 0.0.0.255 (890 matches)
    (192.168.30.0 missing)
actual_root_cause: Standard ACL 1 referenced by the NAT statement does not permit the new Engineering subnet 192.168.30.0/24.

title: Static 1-to-1 NAT Translation Typo in Local IP Address
symptom: External Internet users cannot access public web server at 203.0.113.10.
topology_notes: Internal Web Server IP is 192.168.1.80. Public IP is 203.0.113.10.
show_commands:
R1# show running-config | include ip nat inside source static
ip nat inside source static 192.168.1.88 203.0.113.10

R1# show ip nat translations
Pro Inside global      Inside local       Outside local      Outside global
--- 203.0.113.10       192.168.1.88       ---                ---
actual_root_cause: Static NAT rule maps public IP 203.0.113.10 to 192.168.1.88 instead of the actual web server IP 192.168.1.80.

title: Wireless Client Fails Association Due to SSID Name Case Mismatch
symptom: Laptop-1 cannot associate or see the company Wi-Fi network.
topology_notes: Access Point AP-1 broadcasts SSID 'CorpNet'. Laptop-1 profile configured with 'corpnet'.
show_commands:
AP1# show dot11 associations
(No active associations)

AP1# show running-config | section dot11
dot11 ssid CorpNet
   authentication open
   authentication key-management wpa2
   wpa-psk ascii 7 Cisco12345
!

Laptop-1> show wireless-profile
Profile Name: Work
SSID: corpnet
Security: WPA2-PSK
actual_root_cause: SSID is case-sensitive; client profile is configured with 'corpnet' while AP broadcasts 'CorpNet'.

title: WPA2 Pre-Shared Key Passphrase Mismatch on Client Profile
symptom: Smartphone-1 associates for 1 second then gets immediately disconnected with 4-Way Handshake Failure.
topology_notes: AP configured with WPA2-PSK key 'SecurePass2026!'.
show_commands:
AP1# show logging | include Handshake|Security
%DOT11-4-HANDSHAKE_FAIL: 4-way handshake failed for client 0024.d6a1.b2c3 - MIC failure

AP1# show running-config | include wpa-psk
   wpa-psk ascii 0 SecurePass2026!

Client-1# show wireless-config
SSID: OfficeSecure
Key: Securepass2026!
actual_root_cause: WPA2 Pre-Shared Key mismatch: client has lower-case 'p' ('Securepass2026!') causing 4-Way Handshake MIC authentication failure.

title: Access Point Connected to Access Switchport on Wrong VLAN
symptom: Wireless users successfully associate to AP but receive IP addresses in the Server VLAN (10.0.0.x) instead of Wireless Client VLAN (192.168.40.x).
topology_notes: AP1 connects to Switch SW1 Fa0/12. Expected VLAN is 40.
show_commands:
SW1# show running-config interface FastEthernet0/12
interface FastEthernet0/12
 description Connected to AP-1
 switchport access vlan 10
 switchport mode access
!

SW1# show vlan brief | include 40
40   Wireless-Clients                 active
actual_root_cause: Switch port Fa0/12 connecting AP-1 is assigned to Server VLAN 10 instead of Wireless Client VLAN 40.

title: Guest WLAN Configured with Enterprise 802.1X Instead of Open/PSK
symptom: Visitors attempting to join Guest-WiFi are prompted for corporate RADIUS domain username and password instead of a simple landing page or PSK.
topology_notes: WLC / AP Guest profile.
actual_root_cause: Guest WLAN profile is configured for 802.1X Enterprise authentication instead of Open/WebAuth/PSK.
